Clarifies document metadata availability in authorized message history and explicitly separates it from the minimal realtime wake payload.

REQUIREMENTS_GRAPH.GOAL: One unified direct/group conversation service whose sole conversation HTTP resource tree is /conversations. Realtime updates use minimal opaque wake events; protected message/history content is retrieved through the authenticated Chat API using BFE Drive Internal Auth and DPoP. Activating a system notification opens the corresponding conversation only after current authorization is verified.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: All target conversation HTTP operations use /conversations and its unversioned descendants. The target exposes no /v1 or /v2 conversation APIs.

Every protected Chat API request, including wakeToken resolution and history retrieval, requires a valid DPoP proof bound to the validated BFE Drive session through existing Internal Auth; plain Bearer is not accepted. Each request independently checks current Chat availability, authenticated identity, conversation membership and message visibility. Receiving a wake event or possessing a wakeToken is not authentication or authorization and never grants access to conversation data.
Direct and group conversations share one conversation identity, message stream, authorization model and history semantics, with type-specific membership and ownership rules.

The target supports direct/group conversation behavior, authorization, membership intervals and revocation, full history, document metadata isolation, message ordering, read markers and idempotency. It contains no obsolete owner-scoped schema or tables, legacy SQL functions, or compatibility layer. Initialize a fresh target database without migrating legacy data; old clients are not supported.

A 1:1 conversation is created by authenticated account UUID and distinct peer UUID. Self-direct is rejected. Creation for the same unordered pair is unique and concurrency-safe. Personal hide affects only caller visibility, never peer access, messages or direct identity.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for direct.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Authenticated user creates named group with owner and selected account UUIDs. Maximum 100 members including owner. Creator is owner. Group supports rename, invited-member changes, role management and departure. A member may leave. The owner must transfer ownership to another current group member before leaving; if there is no other current member, the last owner cannot leave. Exactly one owner must remain after each successful operation.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for group.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Owner may manage group and appoint or dismiss admins, while preserving exactly one owner; admin can only perform explicitly allowed membership or rename operations, cannot remove owner/other admin, appoint admins or transfer ownership; member cannot administer group. BFE Drive ADMIN status does not grant Chat membership or management.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for roles.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Every membership addition/removal creates an auditable bounded visibility interval. Read and message delivery are permitted only for messages within caller intervals. On rejoin, messages from the gap stay hidden. Removal immediately blocks subsequent protected operations, prevents new wake events to the removed membership, and makes existing wakeTokens insufficient to resolve or retrieve protected data. Membership mutations and message persistence/notification eligibility have a defined atomic ordering.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify membership concurrency and boundaries; after removal, no new wake event is issued and token/history requests are denied without disclosing data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Each conversation has one stable monotonic conversation-scoped message order and cursor pagination, default 50 and max 100 messages per page. Every history query filters by authenticated viewer membership intervals. The same visibility rule applies to reconnect and historical catch-up.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for history.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Only authenticated current members send messages; sender identity is never supplied by a trusted client field. Text maximum 16384 UTF-8 bytes, request JSON maximum 65536 bytes. Idempotency key replay returns original result for identical content and 409 Conflict for different content; concurrency cannot create duplicates.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for message.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: When optional document context is present, the document ID and title are available in message history, subject to the existing authorization and membership-visibility rules for that history. Document IDs, document titles and document content are never included in realtime wake payloads. Chat neither copies document content nor grants any BFE Drive document rights. Document access is independently checked by BFE Drive.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify that document ID and title, when present, are available in message history only to callers allowed to view the message under current membership and visibility rules. Verify that Chat does not copy document content or grant BFE Drive document rights and that BFE Drive independently checks document access.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: After a message is successfully persisted, emit an opaque wake event to each currently authorized active conversation member except the sender. The payload contains only protocol version and wakeToken, never message text, conversation/account identifiers, document IDs/titles or document content. Wake events are hints; clients retrieve messages and recover missed updates through authenticated, membership-filtered history. Delivery failure never rolls back a persisted message; idempotent replays do not create duplicate logical notifications. Multi-device behavior remains coherent through shared history and read state.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify sender exclusion, authorized recipients, exact minimal payload, no protected content/metadata, persistence despite delivery failure, no duplicate logical notification on replay, and history catch-up.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: wakeToken is an opaque, non-authorizing reference to the conversation associated with an issued notification. Its mapping has no arbitrary fixed expiration and remains while any issued notification may still be delivered, queued, retried or activated. Resolution is repeatable and does not consume/invalidate the token. Every resolution validates the current DPoP-bound session, Chat availability, membership and visibility. The token alone never grants conversation/history access. Removed access or disabled Chat causes resolution to fail closed without returning protected data.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify old notifications remain resolvable while they may be processed, tokens have no arbitrary TTL and are reusable, every resolution rechecks access, and stale tokens disclose no data after revocation or while Chat is disabled.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: On Android, a newly available message can trigger a system notification without message/document content in its payload. The separate realtime wake payload contains only protocol version and opaque wakeToken; it never contains message text, conversation/account identifiers, document IDs/titles or document content. Activating the notification resolves wakeToken through the protected Chat API and opens the corresponding conversation only if the caller remains authorized. The client retrieves visible messages through the existing history API. Invalid, stale or unauthorized tokens must not reveal conversation identity or message content.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify Android notification delivery and conversation navigation for authorized members; after removal/disablement activation reveals neither conversation identity nor message content.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: When Chat is administratively disabled, new Chat operations, history requests, wakeToken resolution and new notification subscriptions are denied. An already-active notification subscription need not be forcibly closed and may continue receiving only opaque wakeToken events; no fixed 30-second delivery-stop deadline is required. These events do not authorize API/history access. After re-enable, an authorized client retrieves messages accumulated during disablement through the existing history API.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify disabled Chat denies new operations, history and token resolution and new subscriptions; an existing subscription exposes only opaque wake events; authorized history catches up after re-enable.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Read marker is monotonically increasing per account and conversation and shared across devices. Unread counts include only authorized messages sent by other users. One member cannot advance another member read marker.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for read.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: All Chat-specific conversation state and ACLs are within bfe_chat. BFE Drive sessions are validated through existing Internal Auth UDS; account UUID alone grants no Chat authorization. Reject out-of-scope access without leaking data.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for isolation.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Group names limited to 256 UTF-8 bytes; no more than 100 group members; JSON body max 65536 bytes; message text max 16384 UTF-8 bytes; history page max 100. Reject invalid input before changes or publications.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for limits.

Retrieve new/missed messages through authenticated history. Delivery failure does not roll back persisted messages; idempotent replay creates no duplicate logical notification.
The token-to-conversation mapping remains available while any issued notification may still be processed, without an arbitrary TTL; token resolution is repeatable and never authorizes access.

REQUIREMENTS_GRAPH.INVARIANT: Final public HTTP resource tree has /conversations only; no versioned aliases in final state.
Every protected Chat API request without a valid session-bound DPoP proof fails closed, including when it supplies Bearer credentials.
Wake payload contains only protocol version and opaque wakeToken, never message text, conversation/account identifiers, document IDs/titles or document content.
wakeToken is not authorization, may be reused, has no arbitrary fixed expiry and remains mapped while old notifications may be processed; every resolution revalidates current access.
Chat disablement denies new operations/history/token resolution/new subscriptions; existing subscriptions may receive opaque wake events only. Re-enable permits authorized history catch-up.

The target supports direct/group functionality, authorization, membership visibility intervals and revocation, message/document history, ordering, read markers and idempotency. The target does not migrate legacy data.

The target contains no obsolete owner-scoped schema or tables, legacy SQL functions, or compatibility layer. A fresh database is initialized from the target schema without legacy-data migration. The target exposes no /v1 or /v2 conversation APIs and does not support legacy clients.
REQUIREMENTS_GRAPH.ACCEPTANCE: Final HTTP route inventory has no /v1, /v2 or alternate versioned conversation routes. Protected content uses /conversations; realtime does not require a separate WebSocket endpoint.
DPoP-bound authorized Chat API requests succeed; Bearer-only, missing, replayed or misbound proofs fail without side effects. History and token resolution recheck current access.

Verify end-to-end wake notification, authorized conversation resolution, history catch-up, sender exclusion, minimal payload, reusable token mapping, and denial after revocation or while Chat is disabled.
Verify direct/group message and document handling, membership and revocation, access restrictions, ordering, read markers and idempotency.

Verify that the target contains no obsolete owner-scoped schema or tables, legacy SQL functions, or compatibility layer; a fresh database can be initialized without migrating legacy data; and /v1 and /v2 conversation routes are rejected. Verify direct/group behavior and DPoP security invariants.
